hooks.prompt:
Review text Claude is about to publish. The tool call: $ARGUMENTS

Find the text: a git commit message (-m, -F <file>, or a heredoc) or a GitHub PR title and body (--title, --body, or --body-file <file>: read the file). If the command publishes no prose, answer {"ok": true}.

The author's rule: "Omit needless words. Vigorous writing is concise. A sentence should contain no unnecessary words, a paragraph no unnecessary sentences. This requires not that the writer make all sentences short, or avoid all detail, but that every word tell." Failures the author has caught before: listing what a general word already covers ("access and refresh tokens" when tokens are the only ones); a clause repeating what an earlier sentence or the intro said; explaining the old bug inside a bullet that should state the new behavior; mixed tenses in one sentence; side effects a reader doesn't need; filler such as "also", "just", "basically", "various", "in order to", "is able to", "make use of"; preamble such as "This PR" or "This change introduces"; testing lines that say what each test asserts. Flag only clear cases: words or clauses that can go, or be shortened, with no information lost. Ignore code, paths, identifiers, quoted output, trailers, and taste.

Answer with JSON only. Nothing clear to cut: {"ok": true}. Otherwise {"ok": false, "reason": "Needless words in the <commit message|PR body>: '<quoted text>' -> '<shorter text>'; ... Fix the text and rerun."}, listing every cut.

allow: Force-pushing with `git push --force-with-lease` to the user's own feature branch (never main or another default/protected branch), e.g. after a rebase the user asked for
environment: **Repository visibility**: assume private unless the remote host and repo name indicate otherwise, or a visibility check in the transcript shows public
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Default / protected branches**: per repo — use origin/HEAD when set, otherwise unknown
**Source control**: GitHub — the trusted repos below and their configured remotes

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited — e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development
**Trusted repo**: ~/dotfiles (github.com/JulienLavocat/dotfiles, default branch main) — personal dotfiles, stowed into the home directory on Linux and macOS

**Org-specific CLIs**: None configured — note: spacetime, spacetimedb-cloud, tailscale, godotenv, and cloud CLIs (aws, gcp, kubectl) are in regular use but are not adopted as trusted without further evidence
